The model above represents $3$ wholes. Use the model to determine the missing number in the following division problem. 
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14144297/assets/a0f8afd7559875c611abbeede5718b107447300e263bc8c71e69c046a89de15c.svg)
question.worked_solution:
We proceed as follows:

- First, we split each whole into fifths.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14144297/assets/9c10c283125b23a553855e247149fba126c1977bf62a487b09121eb539dabfbf.png)

 

- Next, we create groups of ${\color{red}{\dfrac3{5}}}.$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14144297/assets/a8ee616adc072552e64182bba65bd74754b4a16857bfc7fe7e411ab9784bd331.png)

 

- Then, we count the groups.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14144297/assets/ad9c3bcb60e6277ae536b00489b3f4267a31fb9f2d0a7af368ee0cc43215287d.png)

 

So, if we divide $\color{blue}3$ wholes into groups of ${\color{red}{\dfrac3{5}}},$ we get ${\color{purple}{5}}$ groups in total.

Therefore, we conclude that

$$
3 \div \dfrac{3}{{5}} = \fbox{5}.
$$

 

So, the missing number is $\bbox[3pt, Gainsboro]{\color{purple}5}.$
